transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I keep getting up when I really shouldn't. Like, during sprint planning meetings for work, or even on important mortgage calls. I know I should just stay put, but... I'll suddenly feel like I need to get water, or I'll decide I have to go check something in the other room. It's just getting frustrating.
When you feel the urge to get up, is it because you feel physically restless or anxious, or is it because your mind has wandered and you find it hard to sit still?

I think it's mostly that I feel physically restless. Like... even when I’m sitting there looking completely calm on the outside, I get this pressure inside. It just feels like I need to move, or switch tasks, or at least do something with my hands. If I don't, I start to feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, do you remember feeling this same type of restlessness or difficulty sitting still in class?

Yeah, I do. Um, I remember my teachers in elementary school actually having to move my desk a few times. They were constantly reminding me to just stay seated, because I was always popping up out of my chair. I'd also blurt things out and talk before I was called on, or... I'd just rush through my assignments, even when I totally understood the work. So, yeah, it was definitely an issue back then, too.
